author: stevenexus._49168
content:
hi — i built a semaphore-style membership proof that's hash-only
(sha-256 in a risc0 guest, no pairings) so it stays valid after
quantum computers. it's running on a small testnet, ~33 s to prove
on a laptop, <1 s to verify.

two design points i'd value a view on from people who've run
semaphore in the real world:

1. nullifier scope: mine is H(secret ‖ receiver ‖ day_bucket), so a
   member can post about once per day per receiver without being
   linkable across days. i accept ±1 bucket for clock skew, which
   means up to 3 posts around midnight. is there a known better
   shape?
2. small sets: registration is free today, so the set is only as
   honest as its sybils. i'm planning an escrow at the next genesis.
   did semaphore groups find anything cheaper that actually worked?

code: github.com/TET-Network-Foundation/TET-OS
(tet-core/src/tmail/anon.rs, methods/guest). happy to be told i've
reinvented something badly.
